title: Zoom in: how a key gets on the hot list
caption: Pods sample and count locally, a detector merges the counts into a top-K, and the hot list flows back to every pod.

messages.label: GET item:777
messages.note: Every read still goes to the shard at this point.

messages.label: sample 1 in 100
messages.note: Counting every key would cost more than the reads; a sample finds the heavy ones.

messages.label: merge into top-K
messages.note: A key is hot when it is far above the average key, here over 1% of all reads.

messages.label: add item:777, 5 min
messages.note: Entries expire, so a key that cools down drops off by itself.

messages.label: refill item:777
messages.note: Now about one read per pod per second; the rest are served from pod memory.

scenarios.name: Key cools down
scenarios.summary: The drop sells out and traffic falls. Removal needs a lower threshold than adding, or the key flips in and out of the list.

messages.label: 777 under 0.2% for 2 min
messages.note: Two thresholds (add above 1%, remove below 0.2%) stop flapping.

messages.label: GET item:777
messages.note: Back to normal reads with no local copy.

scenarios.name: Detector down
scenarios.summary: Detection is an optimisation. If it stops, existing entries live out their expiry and new hot keys go unnoticed.

messages.label: counts for last 1 s
messages.note: The detector is down; samples go nowhere.

messages.label: keep current hot list
messages.note: Entries already on the list keep working until they expire.

messages.label: GET item:512
messages.note: A newly viral item is not protected: its shard takes every read.

messages.label: local fallback: top keys
messages.note: Mitigation: each pod also keeps its own small top-K, so it can protect itself without the detector.
